title: Chapter 24. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — VIII: Gaura's night sleep; Nityananda
html:
Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 24: the end of GPT section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya" — the songs on Gaura's night sleep (GPT1 pp. 362–365, nos. 55–63, 65: the companions gaze at the sleeping Lord and do not dare to wake Him), then section 6.1 "Nityananda" (GPT1 pp. 414–439) — all padas signed Narahari (nos. 10, 26, 64–69, 71–78, 80, 81: the advent at Ekachakra, the first meeting with the Lord, the coming to Gauda, Panihati, Khardaha, the wedding, praises), with the addition of the pada on Balarama's rasa manifested by Nityananda (section 5.1, no. 44). The signatures in both sections were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the Gaura-charita-chintamani (GCC, kiranas 2–4) and the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) were read continuously at the relevant places. Not translated (outside the appendix): 5.2 nos. 54, 64 and 6.1 nos. 6, 11, 19, 70, 79 — signed Ghanashyama; the other padas of section 6.1 are by other poets (Atmarama, Govinda Dasa, Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa, Lochana, Jnanadasa, Vasu Ghosha, Balarama Dasa, Kanu Dasa, Raya Ananta and others; some were translated earlier). The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places by the scan), collated with GPT2, the GCC (ed. 1947), the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gita-chandrodaya; the PK, KGC and PS were checked. On the ashtakaliya as eternal lila and on the Lord's sleep see note 36 of chapter 22. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.

1. Narahari — "ko baraṇaba bara gaura uttāna śayana…" (GPT1 p. 362, section 5.2, no. 55; GCC)

The end of the night: Gaura sleeps on His back; the poet describes His form — the shining limbs, the face outshining autumn moons, the earrings, lips, teeth, the necklaces on His chest, the folded hands: as if even in sleep He were pleading with an offended beloved. Raga not specified ("yathārāga"). Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.1

কো বরণব বর গৌর উত্তান শয়ন শোভা সুখকারী ।
ঝলকত অঙ্গ সুবলিত ললিত থির দামিনী-পুঞ্জ-পুঞ্জ-মদহারী ॥

ko baraṇaba bara gaura uttāna śayana śobhā sukhakārī |
jhalakata aṅga subalita lalita thira dāminī-puñja-puñja-madahārī ||

ko — who; baraṇaba — will describe; bara gaura — fair Gaura; uttāna śayana — lying on His back; śobhā — beauty; sukhakārī — delightful; jhalakata — shine; aṅga — limbs; subalita — shapely; lalita — graceful; thira dāminī — steady lightning; puñja-puñja — of hosts; mada-hārī — robbing of pride

1.1Who can describe the delightful beauty of fair Gaura sleeping on His back?
His shapely, graceful limbs shine, robbing hosts of steady lightning of their pride.

শরদ-সুধাকর-নিকর বিনির্জিত যুবতী-বিজয় মুখ মধুরিম জ্যোতি ।
শ্রুতি অতি বিমল গণ্ড মণ্ডিত নব কুণ্ডল অতুল জড়িত মণি মোতি ॥

śarada-sudhākara-nikara binirjita yubatī-bijaya mukha madhurima jyoti |
śruti ati bimala gaṇḍa maṇḍita naba kuṇḍala atula jaṛita maṇi moti ||

śarada-sudhākara-nikara — hosts of autumn moons; binirjita — defeated; yubatī-bijaya — conquering young maidens; mukha — of the face; madhurima jyoti — sweet light; śruti — ears; ati bimala gaṇḍa — clear cheeks; maṇḍita — adorned; naba kuṇḍala — with new earrings; atula — matchless; jaṛita maṇi moti — set with gems and pearls

1.2The sweet light of His face, which conquers young maidens, defeats hosts of autumn moons; His ears and clear cheeks are adorned with new earrings, matchless, set with gems and pearls.

বিম্ব অরুণ-কর-কদন বদন-ছদ কিঞ্চিদ মিলন রুচির রুচিপূর ।
বিকসত দন্তকিরণ সিত সুন্দর তারকবৃন্দ কুন্দ রহু দূর ॥

bimba aruṇa-kara-kadana badana-chada kiñcida milana rucira rucipūra |
bikasata dantakiraṇa sita sundara tārakabṛnda kunda rahu dūra ||

bimba — the bimba fruit; aruṇa-kara — the rays of dawn; kadana — putting to shame; badana-chada — lips; kiñcida milana — slightly closed; rucira — lovely; ruci-pūra — full of radiance; bikasata — gleams; danta-kiraṇa — the light of the teeth; sita sundara — white, beautiful; tāraka-bṛnda — stars; kunda — jasmine; rahu dūra — stay far away

1.3His lips, putting to shame the bimba fruit and the rays of dawn, are slightly closed, lovely, full of radiance; the white, beautiful light of His teeth gleams — the stars and the jasmine stay far behind.

প্রসর বক্ষ পরি হার প্রচুর তহি কর করযুক্ত লসত অনিবার ।
নরহরি ভণ অনুভব ন হোত বুঝি মানিনী নিকট করত পরিহার ॥

prasara bakṣa pari hāra pracura tahi kara karayukta lasata anibāra |
narahari bhaṇa anubhaba na hota bujhi māninī nikaṭa karata parihāra ||

prasara bakṣa pari — on the broad chest; hāra pracura — many necklaces; tahi — there; kara kara-yukta — hands joined palm to palm; lasata anibāra — rest unmoving; narahari bhaṇa — Narahari says; anubhaba na hota — cannot be grasped; bujhi — surely; māninī nikaṭa — before an offended beloved; karata parihāra — pleads

1.4On His broad chest are many necklaces, and on it His hands, joined palm to palm, rest unmoving. Narahari says: this cannot be grasped — surely He is pleading before an offended beloved.2

"5.3" — wrongly). GCC — kirana 2 (the "pastimes on the couch" in the last part of the night), pada 18: before it Gadadhara, waking first, serves the Lord's feet, and He turns onto His back (padas 15–16); then comes a pada of Ghanashyama (GPT no. 54) and this one. Readings: 1.1 GCC "bara gaura sarasa uttāna śayana"; "dāminī-puñja" ("of lightning") — GPT1 and GPT2 "yāminī puñja" ("of nights"), a misprint; the GCC reading is adopted; 1.4 GCC "anubhaba na hota" (GPT "anubhava nohata"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya. B. On the ashtakaliya and on the Lord's sleep see note 36 of chapter 22. with Radha who is in mana (offended pride) — the folded hands betray His inner mood (cf. in the same kirana of the GCC, pada 13: in sleep Gaura calls upon "the crown of beautiful women" to wake). "Which conquers young maidens" is a stock formula of the lyric on Krishna's all-attractive beauty (cf. note 7 of chapter 23); here it refers to Gaura as Krishna Himself.

2. Narahari — "ki kahaba gaura śayana anupāma…" (GPT1 pp. 362–363, no. 56; GCC)

Gaura's matchless sleep: His limbs shine like Kama embodied; His body is soft as fresh butter — it seems to melt on the couch; His breathing gently lifts His belly, as the Malaya wind stirs the waves of a river on Sumeru. The poet prays that the Lord may so rest on the couch of his heart. Raga lalita. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.3

কি কহব গৌর শয়ন অনুপাম ।
সুবলিত অঙ্গ অঙ্গ ঝলকত জনু বিলসিত সোই মূরতিময় কাম ॥ ধ্রু ॥

ki kahaba gaura śayana anupāma |
subalita aṅga aṅga jhalakata janu bilasita soi mūratimaya kāma || dhru ||

ki kahaba — what shall I say; gaura śayana — of Gaura's sleep; anupāma — matchless; subalita aṅga aṅga — each shapely limb; jhalakata — shines; janu — as if; bilasita — displayed his play; soi — himself; muratimaya kāma — Kama in visible form

2.1What shall I say of Gaura's matchless sleep! Each of His shapely limbs shines — as if Kama himself, in visible form, were displaying his play here.

কনক-ক্ষীরোদদধি মন্থন নব নবনী-পিণ্ডসম কোমল কায় ।
অতি অপরূপ ইহ তপনতাপ বিনু শেজ উপরি জনু জাত মিলায় ॥

kanaka-kṣīrodadadhi manthana naba nabanī-piṇḍasama komala kāya |
ati aparūpa iha tapanatāpa binu śeja upari janu jāta milāya ||

kanaka-kṣīroda-dadhi — a golden ocean of milk; manthana — churned from; naba nabanī-piṇḍa-sama — like a lump of fresh butter; komala kāya — soft body; ati aparūpa iha — wonder of wonders; tapana-tāpa binu — without the sun's heat; śeja upari — on the couch; janu — as if; jāta milāya — melts away

2.2His body is soft as a lump of fresh butter churned from a golden ocean of milk;
and, wonder of wonders, without the sun's heat it seems to melt upon the couch.

অলসে অবশ মৃদু চলত নিশাসহি উচ নীচ হোয়ত উদর উজোর ।
মলয় পবন জনু পরশ সুমেরুসু সরিত তরঙ্গ বহত বহু থোর ॥

alase abaśa mṛdu calata niśāsahi uca nīca hoyata udara ujora |
malaya pabana janu paraśa sumerusu sarita taraṅga bahata bahu thora ||

alase — in languor; abaśa — limp; mṛdu calata niśāsahi — breathing softly; uca nīca hoyata — rises and falls; udara ujora — the radiant belly; malaya pabana — the Malaya wind; janu — as if; paraśa — touching; sumerusu — Sumeru; sarita taraṅga — the river's waves; bahata — drives; bahu thora — gentle, small

2.3Languid, limp, He breathes softly, and His radiant belly rises and falls —
as if the Malaya wind, touching Sumeru, drove the quiet waves of its river.

বচনক দূর বিরচব কৌন পুনি নিরখত নয়ন তৃপিত নহি হোয় ।
নরহরি ভণ মঝু হৃদয়-তল্প কব বিলসব ঐছে দেয়ব সুখ মোয় ॥

bacanaka dūra biracaba kauna puni nirakhata nayana tṛpita nahi hoya |
narahari bhaṇa majhu hṛdaya-talpa kaba bilasaba aiche deyaba sukha moya ||

bacanaka dūra — beyond words; biracaba kauna — who will compose; puni — and; nirakhata nayana — the eyes, gazing; tṛpita nahi hoya — are not sated; narahari bhaṇa — Narahari says; majhu hṛdaya-talpa — on the couch of my heart; kaba — when; bilasaba aiche — will so recline; deyaba sukha moya — will give me joy

2.4Words cannot convey it — who could compose it? However long one looks, the eyes are never sated. Narahari says: when will He so recline on the couch of my heart and give me joy?4

("lalita rāga"; preceded by a description of the chamber and the couch). Readings: 2.2 GCC "kṣīrododadhi" ("ocean of milk"; GPT "kṣīroda dadhi"); 2.4 GCC "biracaba" (GPT1 "viracana"). Under line 2.3 GPT1 has an editor's note on the reading "bilāse" (not reproduced). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B. enchants even the god of love (Bhag. 10.32.2), and Gaura's beauty is not mundane: the poet prays not for anything sensual but that the Lord may reign in his heart. Sumeru is the golden mountain — an image of Gaura's golden body.

3. Narahari — "ki kaba analpa talpa jhalakata ati…" (GPT1 p. 363, no. 57; GCC)

Gaura's couch: spacious, spotless as autumn, fashioned by Kama himself; the white pillows are like blocks of Kailasa and the stilled waves of the Ganga; heaps of flowers, a painted canopy of moonbeams, a silver frame set with gold and gems. Raga lalita. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli (the text is obscure in places).5

কি কব অনল্প তল্প ঝলকত অতি শরদ কাল সম বিরহিত মলিনা ।
সুরপতি-স্বপন-অগোচর অপরূপ রচিত মনোজ্ঞ মনোভব বলিনা ॥

ki kaba analpa talpa jhalakata ati śarada kāla sama birahita malinā |
surapati-svapana-agocara aparūpa racita manojña manobhaba balinā ||

ki kaba — what shall I say; analpa talpa — the spacious couch; jhalakata ati — shines beyond measure; śarada kāla sama — like the autumn season; birahita malinā — free of stain; surapati-svapana-agocara — beyond the dreams of the king of the gods; aparūpa — wondrous; racita — fashioned; manojña — charming; manobhaba balinā — by mighty Manobhava (Kama)

3.1What shall I say! The spacious couch shines beyond measure, spotless as the autumn season; wondrous, beyond even the dreams of the king of the gods, a charming work of mighty Manobhava.

আলস-ধর জন-লালস-কর বর বালিস বিলসত জগত অদৃশ রে ।
হরগিরি-খণ্ড অখণ্ড সদ্য দধি-পিণ্ড গঙ্গ-থির-তরঙ্গ সদৃশ রে ॥

ālasa-dhara jana-lālasa-kara bara bālisa bilasata jagata adṛśa re |
haragiri-khaṇḍa akhaṇḍa sadya dadhi-piṇḍa gaṅga-thira-taraṅga sadṛśa re ||

ālasa-dhara — full of languor; jana-lālasa-kara — awakening desire in people; bara bālisa — lovely pillows; bilasata — shine; jagata adṛśa — unlike anything in the world; haragiri-khaṇḍa — blocks of Hara's mountain; akhaṇḍa — whole; sadya dadhi-piṇḍa — lumps of fresh curd; gaṅga-thira-taraṅga — the stilled waves of the Ganga; sadṛśa — like

3.2Lovely pillows, full of languor and awakening desire, shine — there is nothing like them in the world: like blocks of Hara's mountain, whole lumps of fresh curd, the stilled waves of the Ganga.

তহি বন্ধুরে করবীর কুন্দ কেতকী কনকাব্জ জাতী কৃতনয়না ।
তনু অব যব সব সুমনগণ ঝটিত অনুভব ন হোই গৌরহরি-শয়না ॥

tahi bandhure karabīra kunda ketakī kanakābja jātī kṛtanayanā |
tanu aba yaba saba sumanagaṇa jhaṭita anubhaba na hoi gaurahari-śayanā ||

tahi — on it; bandhure — in heaps; karabīra, kunda, ketakī — karavira, kunda, ketaki; kanakābja — golden lotuses; jātī — jasmine; kṛta-nayanā — arranged (?); tanu — tender; aba yaba saba sumanagaṇa — when all the flowers; jhaṭita — are strewn (?); anubhaba na hoi — one cannot tell; gaurahari-śayanā — that it is Gaurahari's couch

3.3On it, in heaps — karavira, kunda, ketaki, golden lotuses, jasmine; and when all their tender flowers are strewn, one can no longer tell that this is Gaurahari's couch.

বুঝি শশী-কর-পটে বিরচি চিত্র বিহি মন্দির দেবে দেওল বহু যতনে ।
নরহরি ভণব সুমতি উরথিত ইহ রজত-চতুষ্কি জটিত হেম রতনে ॥

bujhi śaśī-kara-paṭe biraci citra bihi mandira debe deola bahu yatane |
narahari bhaṇaba sumati urathita iha rajata-catuṣki jaṭita hema ratane ||

bujhi — as if; śaśī-kara-paṭe — on a cloth of moonbeams; biraci citra — painting pictures; bihi — the Creator; mandira — into the chamber; debe — of the Lord (?); deola — brought; bahu yatane — with great care; narahari bhaṇaba — Narahari will say; sumati urathita — rises beautifully (?); iha — this; rajata-catuṣki — a silver frame; jaṭita hema ratane — studded with gold and gems

3.4It is as if the Creator painted pictures on a cloth of moonbeams and with great care brought it into the Lord's chamber; Narahari will say: this couch rises on a silver frame studded with gold and gems.6

right after no. 56). Readings: 3.2 GCC "ālasa-dhara jana lālasa-kara bara bālisa" (GPT "ālasa dhara jala lālasa karabara bālisa"; translated after the GCC: "… awakening desire in people"); 3.3 GCC "bandhuṇa", "kṛta nayana", "sumanagaṇa" (GPT "bandhure", "kṛtanayanā", "samana gana"); 3.4 GCC "deyala", "bhaṇaba sumati" (the sense of "sumati urathita" is unclear; taken as "rises beautifully"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B. "Gaura-Hari" is Krishna Himself, not a worldly prince. Hara's mountain is Kailasa, the white abode of Shiva; curd and the waves of the Ganga are images of whiteness.

4. Narahari — "mari mari gaura-mūrati aparūpa…" (GPT1 p. 363, no. 58; GCC)

One of the companions, looking at the sleeping Lord: wondrous is Gaura's form; alas that I have only two eyes; I keep this treasure in my heart; every morning I see Him, but I have never seen such sleep — shall I wake Him today? Raga vibhasa. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.7

মরি মরি গৌর-মূরতি অপরূপ । ভুবন-বিমোহন মনমথ-ভূপ ॥

mari mari gaura-mūrati aparūpa | bhubana-bimohana manamatha-bhūpa ||

mari mari — ah, ah; gaura-mūrati — Gaura's form; aparūpa — wondrous; bhubana-bimohana — enchanter of the world; manamatha-bhūpa — king Manmatha

4.1Ah, ah! Wondrous is Gaura's form — the enchanter of the world, king Manmatha.

কি করব অগণিত নয়ন না ভেল । দারুণ দৈব দরশে দুখ দেল ॥

ki karaba agaṇita nayana nā bhela | dāruṇa daiba daraśe dukha dela ||

ki karaba — what can I do; agaṇita nayana — countless eyes; nā bhela — were not given; dāruṇa daiba — cruel fate; daraśe — in letting me see; dukha dela — gave grief

4.2What can I do — I was not given countless eyes! Cruel fate, letting me see Him, gave me grief as well.

রাখি হৃদয় ভরি ইহ অভিলাষ । অমূল রতন সম না করি প্রকাশ ॥

rākhi hṛdaya bhari iha abhilāṣa | amūla ratana sama nā kari prakāśa ||

rākhi — I keep; hṛdaya bhari — filling the heart; iha abhilāṣa — this longing; amūla ratana sama — like a priceless jewel; nā kari prakāśa — I do not reveal

4.3I keep this longing, filling my heart with it; like a priceless jewel I reveal it to no one.

কৌনে গঢ়ল তনু-বলনি সুঠাম । মঝু সরবস এ জগতে অনুপাম ॥

kaune gaṛhala tanu-balani suṭhāma | majhu sarabasa e jagate anupāma ||

kaune gaṛhala — who sculpted; tanu-balani — the body, the frame; suṭhāma — graceful; majhu sarabasa — all my wealth; e jagate anupāma — matchless in this world

4.4Who sculpted His body, this graceful frame? It is all my wealth, matchless in the world.

অনুদিন রজনীশেষে হাম পেখি । ঐছন শয়ন কবহুঁ নাহি দেখি ॥

anudina rajanīśeṣe hāma pekhi | aichana śayana kabahum̐ nāhi dekhi ||

anudina — every day; rajanī-śeṣe — at the end of the night; hāma pekhi — I see; aichana śayana — such sleep; kabahum̐ nāhi dekhi — I have never seen

4.5Every day at the end of the night I see Him, but such sleep I have never seen.

তাহে বুঝলুঁ নব ঘুম বিরাজ । নরহরি ইথে কি জাগাওব আজ ॥

tāhe bujhalum̐ naba ghuma birāja | narahari ithe ki jāgāoba āja ||

tāhe — therefore; bujhalum̐ — I understand; naba ghuma — a new sleep; birāja — reigns; narahari — Narahari; ithe — then; ki jāgāoba — shall I wake; āja — now

4.6So I understand: a new, unheard-of sleep reigns. Narahari: shall I wake Him now?8

("ko 'pi ca — bibhāṣa rāgeṇa", "and another [said] in raga vibhasa"): after a pada describing the sleeper (3.3) the GCC puts padas 4–7 into the mouths of various companions who have come to the Lord's chamber at dawn. The readings differ insignificantly (4.5 GCC "kavahi"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B. the Lord is absorbed in lila more deeply than usual; the companion hesitates to wake Him, not daring to interrupt His bliss.

5. Narahari — "dhani dhani āju rajanī dhani lekhi…" (GPT1 p. 363, no. 59; GCC)

Another companion: blessed is this night! The Lord, greedy for sankirtana, did not close His eyes at night, speaking of Vraja in His former mood — and now He has sunk into a matchless sleep and speaks nectarean words in it; it is already dawn, and He does not wake. Raga bhairava. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.9

ধনি ধনি আজু রজনী ধনি লেখি ।
সংকীর্তন-রস-লম্পট পহুঁ কর ঐছন শয়ন কবহিঁ নাহি দেখি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

dhani dhani āju rajanī dhani lekhi |
